svg.text: No races by construction — who writes what, and how each kind of data crosses between the threads (AS BUILT)
Rule: each world has ONE writer. The UI reads only its own world A; the simulation reads only S. Every crossing uses one of the mechanisms below — NONE takes a lock (R-4216 / R-4217).
WORLD S — written ONLY by the SIM thread and its pool
(own entity directly, other entities by command)
HOW IT CROSSES
WORLD A — written ONLY by the MAIN thread
(the pull copies the newest staging buffer in)
SIM → UI (the sim publishes at the tick's end into a free buffer; the UI pulls at its frame start)
components the map, 3-D, overlays draw
STAGED — a mask of types (the ACTIVE gizmo layers), all rows
the same tables in A
the selected / inspected units' components
STAGED — rows of the selected entities, types outside the mask
their rows in A (panels, inspector)
small per-tick singletons: GlobalTime, traces
STAGED BY VALUE (a refilled managed one value-copied — N-9)
their copies in A
values only the sim can compute: save gate, args
READOUTS — built after the tick, only when changed, staged
the UI's readouts (no sim object)
changing service state: cluster cache, clock
IMMUTABLE VIEW published — one atomic reference swap (0.01 ms)
the latest view (no lock)
shared objects: terrain, geo, TKB, behaviours, navmesh
SHARED BY REFERENCE — immutable, or replaced in ONE atomic swap
the same object, old or new, never half
native memory: the road graph
LEASED — the old version lives until the last reader lets go
a lease per publish
logs, edit outcomes, undo steps, squad reports
PACKET FIFO — tick-tagged, drained in order, none lost on a skip
A's logs, the ONE undo history
events on S's buses (incl. the orchestration bus)
BUS PAIR — down per tick exactly once; the UI's publishes ride up
A's bus + the UI's own read models
remote nodes' gizmo streams (CGF, SimHost …)
RECEIVED over the network, published to the map — triple buffer
the map draws them with A's own gizmos
UI → SIM (the UI never writes S)
edits: move, delete, spawn, orders, rules
JOB — the ONE SimJobQueue, drained between ticks; the existing write code runs on S; refused ⇒ the outcome
applied by the sim thread
drag / rotate / place
a GHOST in A every frame — the drop ONE job via the shared write router; refused ⇒ snap back
applied by the sim thread
run controls · sim-side HTTP · review (R-4220 ⏳)
JOBS — the clock lives with the simulation; UI-side routes read the shown world
applied by the sim thread
undo / redo
JOBS — the recorder on S takes the before-snapshot; the history stays on the UI
applied by the sim thread
STAYS ON ONE SIDE — never crosses
brain memory, sensors, EQS, physics, the
node frame, the orchestrator, recording
a reader on the other side asks through a command or the HTTP API (answered at a tick boundary)
selection, menus, camera, order form,
effects, panel layout — written directly

✔ READS ARE READS: a managed read never stamps (R-4210) · managed components immutable, replaced whole · the STRICT world guard: 0 hits over the full 1 000-man session (no S read off the sim thread, no A write by the sim)
INSIDE THE TICK: OWN entity direct · others by command in the batch's buffer, played in batch order · their data from the tick-start view · follow-ups in batch order · HROT_READ_CHECK
The gizmos — the WHOLE gizmo block runs on the main thread over world A (R-4211: no split by kind)
ONE BLOCK — main thread, every frame
all 75 registered gizmos: overlays (navmesh, cover,
EQS, brain debug, routes, names, traces …), tools
(drag, rotate, editors, pickers, RTS mode, box select)
and UI gizmos — one module, one place, as today
pick boxes, pickers and selection stay together
(CE-259r: they hit-test THIS frame's boxes)
maintained as one thing — no per-kind homes
WHAT IT READS — world A
the overlays read A's copies; the S→A mask follows
the ACTIVE gizmo layers: nothing when none is shown,
≈ 57 types / 1.3 ms with all on, usually just labels
content still changes only when S ticks — drawn
at the frame rate from the latest copy
cost moved off the SIM tick: ≈ 4.4–5.5 ms
(it now runs on the main thread's ~16 ms frame)
WHAT IT WRITES — jobs only
input → the tool's FSM every frame → a GHOST in A
→ the commit is ONE JOB to S
✔ built: the preview is a ghost re-applied after
each pull; a refused commit snaps back
headless nodes (CGF, SimHost) have no main-thread
presentation: their gizmo stream is produced in
their own tick and sent over the network, as today
threaded --mode all: an unstaged subsystem draws nothing
the gizmo MODULE also runs non-gizmo world WRITERS (action dispatch: Delete / LoadZone, effect + wreck spawn, lifespan) — those are simulation and stay in the tick
staged by the sim into a free buffer, pulled by the UI — no lock
published / shared — an atomic reference swap or a lease, no lock
a job on the SimJobQueue — the UI's only way into S
